<h1 id="metal-api">Metal API v1.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

# Introduction
Equinix Metal provides a RESTful HTTP API which can be reached at <https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1>. This document describes the API and how to use it.

The API allows you to programmatically interact with all
of your Equinix Metal resources, including devices, networks, addresses, organizations,
projects, and your user account. Every feature of the Equinix Metal web interface is accessible through the API.

The API docs are generated from the Equinix Metal OpenAPI specification and are officially hosted at <https://metal.equinix.com/developers/api>.

# Common Parameters

The Equinix Metal API uses a few methods to minimize network traffic and improve throughput. These parameters are not used in all API calls, but are used often enough to warrant their own section. Look for these parameters in the documentation for the API calls that support them.

## Pagination

Pagination is used to limit the number of results returned in a single request. The API will return a maximum of 100 results per page. To retrieve additional results, you can use the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

The `page` parameter is used to specify the page number. The first page is `1`. The `per_page` parameter is used to specify the number of results per page. The maximum number of results differs by resource type.

## Sorting

Where offered, the API allows you to sort results by a specific field. To sort results use the `sort_by` query parameter with the root level field name as the value. The `sort_direction` parameter is used to specify the sort direction, either either `asc` (ascending) or `desc` (descending).

## Filtering

Filtering is used to limit the results returned in a single request. The API supports filtering by certain fields in the response. To filter results, you can use the field as a query parameter.

For example, to filter the IP list to only return public IPv4 addresses, you can filter by the `type` field, as in the following request:

```sh
curl -H 'X-Auth-Token: my_authentication_token' \
  https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/id/ips?type=public_ipv4
```

Only IP addresses with the `type` field set to `public_ipv4` will be returned.

## Searching

Searching is used to find matching resources using multiple field comparissons. The API supports searching in resources that define this behavior. Currently the search parameter is only available on devices, ssh_keys, api_keys and memberships endpoints.

To search resources you can use the `search` query parameter.

## Include and Exclude

For resources that contain references to other resources, sucha as a Device that refers to the Project it resides in, the Equinix Metal API will returns `href` values (API links) to the associated resource.

```json
{
  ...
  "project": {
    "href": "/metal/v1/projects/f3f131c8-f302-49ef-8c44-9405022dc6dd"
  }
}
```

If you're going need the project details, you can avoid a second API request.  Specify the contained `href` resources and collections that you'd like to have included in the response using the `include` query parameter.

For example:

```sh
curl -H 'X-Auth-Token: my_authentication_token' \
  https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/user?include=projects
```

The `include` parameter is generally accepted in `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, and `PATCH` requests where `href` resources are presented.

To have multiple resources include, use a comma-separated list (e.g. `?include=emails,projects,memberships`).

```sh
curl -H 'X-Auth-Token: my_authentication_token' \
  https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/user?include=emails,projects,memberships
```

You may also include nested associations up to three levels deep using dot notation (`?include=memberships.projects`):

```sh
curl -H 'X-Auth-Token: my_authentication_token' \
  https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/user?include=memberships.projects
```

To exclude resources, and optimize response delivery, use the `exclude` query parameter. The `exclude` parameter is generally accepted in `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, and `PATCH` requests for fields with nested object responses. When excluded, these fields will be replaced with an object that contains only an `href` field.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1">https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1</a>

# Authentication

* API Key (x_auth_token)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Auth-Token**, in: header. HTTP header containing the User or Project API key that will be used to authenticate the request.

<h1 id="metal-api-authentication">Authentication</h1>

Nearly all of the endpoints in the API require authentication. Authentication is performed by providing an authentication token (interchangeably referred to as an API key) in the `X-Auth-Token` HTTP request header.

<!-- ReDoc-Inject: <security-definitions> -->

User API keys can be obtained by creating them in the Equinix Metal Portal or by using the [Create a User API Key](#operation/createAPIKey) endpoint.

Project API keys can also be obtained by creating them in the Equinix Metal Portal or by using the [Create a Project API Key](#operation/createProjectAPIKey) endpoint. Project API keys are scoped to a single project and can only be used to access resources within that project.

For example, to use an authenticated API token, you would make a request like the following:

```bash
curl -H 'X-Auth-Token: my_authentication_token' \
  https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/user/api-keys
```

Applications can take advantage of the Equinix Metal API and API keys to perform any of the actions that can be performed in the Equinix Metal Portal. For example, you can use the API to create and manage devices, projects, and other resources.

API keys can be deleted without affecting any of the resources created with them. Access to applications using the API can be revoked by deleting the API key used to authenticate the application.


<a href="https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/accounts/users/#api-keys">External documentation</a>

## Delete the API key

<a id="opIddeleteAPIKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/api-keys/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /api-keys/{id}`

Deletes the API key.

<h3 id="delete-the-api-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|API Key UUID|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "errors": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "errors": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-the-api-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|no content|None|
|401|Unauthorized|unauthorized|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|not found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Create an API key for a project.

<a id="opIdcreateProjectAPIKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/api-keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "read_only": true,
```

<h1 id="metal-api-batches">Batches</h1>

Manage device batches. See project endpoints to list batches for a particular project. Check out the product docs to learn more about [Batch Deployment](https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/deploy/batch-deployment/).


<a href="https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/deploy/batch-deployment/">External documentation</a>

## Create a devices batch

<a id="opIdcreateDeviceBatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/devices/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "batches": [
      null,
      null
```

## Requesting bgp config

<a id="opIdrequestBgpConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/bgp-configs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

    "deployment_type": "local",
    "asn": 65000,
    "md5": "md5"
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{id}/bgp-configs`

Requests to enable bgp configuration for a project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "use_case": "use_case",
  "deployment_type": "local",
  "asn": 65000,
  "md5": "md5"
}
```

<h3 id="requesting-bgp-config-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Project UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[BgpConfigRequestInput](#schemabgpconfigrequestinput)|true|BGP config Request to create|
|» asn|body|integer|true|Autonomous System Number for local BGP deployment.|
|» deployment_type|body|[BgpConfigRequestInput_deployment_type](#schemabgpconfigrequestinput_deployment_type)|true|Wether the BGP deployment is local or global. Local deployments are configured immediately. Global deployments will need to be reviewed by Equinix Metal engineers.|
|» md5|body|string|false|The plaintext password to share between BGP neighbors as an MD5 checksum:<br>* must be 10-20 characters long<br>* may not include punctuation<br>* must be a combination of numbers and letters<br>* must contain at least one lowercase, uppercase, and digit character<br>|
|» use_case|body|string|false|A use case explanation (necessary for global BGP request review).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» deployment_type|local|
|» deployment_type|global|

```json
  ]
}
```

```json
  ]
}
```

```json
  ]
}
```

## Update interconnection

<a id="opIdupdateInterconnection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/connections/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "mode": "standard",
    "name": "name",
    "description": "description",
    "redundancy": "redundancy",
    "contact_email": "contact_email",
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /connections/{connection_id}`

Update the details of a interconnection

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mode": "standard",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "redundancy": "redundancy",
  "contact_email": "contact_email",
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-interconnection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connection_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Interconnection UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[InterconnectionUpdateInput](#schemainterconnectionupdateinput)|true|Updated interconnection details|
|» contact_email|body|string|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» mode|body|[Interconnection_mode](#schemainterconnection_mode)|false|The mode of the interconnection (only relevant to Dedicated Ports). Shared connections won't have this field. Can be either 'standard' or 'tunnel'.<br>  The default mode of an interconnection on a Dedicated Port is 'standard'. The mode can only be changed when there are no associated virtual circuits on the interconnection.<br>  In tunnel mode, an 802.1q tunnel is added to a port to send/receive double tagged packets from server instances.|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» redundancy|body|string|false|Updating from 'redundant' to 'primary' will remove a secondary port, while updating from 'primary' to 'redundant' will add one.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|standard|
|» mode|tunnel|

`POST /connections/{connection_id}/ports/{port_id}/virtual-circuits`

Create a new Virtual Circuit on a Dedicated Port. To create a regular Virtual Circuit, specify a Virtual Network record and an NNI VLAN value. To create a VRF-based Virtual Circuit, specify the VRF ID and subnet, along with the NNI VLAN value.

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-device-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|ok|[Device](#schemadevice)|
|401|Unauthorized|unauthorized|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|not found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Update the device

<a id="opIdupdateDevice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/devices/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "userdata": "userdata",
    "hostname": "hostname",
    "spot_instance": true,
    "network_frozen": true,
    "description": "description",
    "firmware_set_id": "firmware_set_id",
    "always_pxe": true,
    "billing_cycle": "billing_cycle",
    "customdata": {
      "key": ""
    },
    "ipxe_script_url": "ipxe_script_url",
    "locked": true,
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /devices/{id}`

Updates the device.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "userdata": "userdata",
  "hostname": "hostname",
  "spot_instance": true,
  "network_frozen": true,
  "description": "description",
  "firmware_set_id": "firmware_set_id",
  "always_pxe": true,
  "billing_cycle": "billing_cycle",
  "customdata": {
    "key": ""
  },
  "ipxe_script_url": "ipxe_script_url",
  "locked": true,
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-device-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Device UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[DeviceUpdateInput](#schemadeviceupdateinput)|true|Device to update|
|» always_pxe|body|boolean|false|none|

## Perform an action

<a id="opIdperformAction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/devices/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "preserve_data": true,
    "force_delete": true,
    "operating_system": "ubuntu_22_04",
    "ipxe_script_url": "ipxe_script_url",
    "type": null,
    "deprovision_fast": true
  }'
```

`POST /devices/{id}/actions`

Performs an action for the given device.  Possible actions include: power_on, power_off, reboot, reinstall, and rescue (reboot the device into rescue OS.)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "preserve_data": true,
  "force_delete": true,
  "operating_system": "ubuntu_22_04",
  "ipxe_script_url": "ipxe_script_url",
  "type": null,
  "deprovision_fast": true
}
```

<h3 id="perform-an-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Device UUID|
|body|body|[DeviceActionInput](#schemadeviceactioninput)|true|Action to perform|
|» type|body|[DeviceActionInput_type](#schemadeviceactioninput_type)|true|Action to perform. See Device.actions for possible actions.|
|» force_delete|body|boolean|false|May be required to perform actions under certain conditions|
|» deprovision_fast|body|boolean|false|When type is `reinstall`, enabling fast deprovisioning will bypass full disk wiping.|
|» preserve_data|body|boolean|false|When type is `reinstall`, preserve the existing data on all disks except the operating-system disk.|
|» operating_system|body|string|false|When type is `reinstall`, use this `operating_system` (defaults to the current `operating system`)|
|» ipxe_script_url|body|string|false|When type is `reinstall`, use this `ipxe_script_url` (`operating_system` must be `custom_ipxe`, defaults to the current `ipxe_script_url`)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|power_on|
|» type|power_off|
|» type|reboot|
|» type|rescue|
|» type|reinstall|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "errors": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "errors": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "errors": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="perform-an-action-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|accepted|None|
|401|Unauthorized|unauthorized|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|not found|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|unprocessable entity|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve all devices of an organization

<a id="opIdfindOrganizationDevices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/organizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/devices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /organizations/{id}/devices`

Provides a collection of devices for a given organization.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-devices-of-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Organization UUID|
|search|query|string|false|Search by hostname, description, short_id, reservation short_id, tags, plan name, plan slug, facility code, facility name, operating system name, operating system slug, IP addresses.|
|categories|query|[[findOrganizationDevices_categories_parameter_inner](#schemafindorganizationdevices_categories_parameter_inner)]|false|Filter by plan category|
|facility|query|string|false|Filter by device facility|
|hostname|query|string|false|Filter by partial hostname|
|reserved|query|boolean|false|Filter only reserved instances. When set to true, only include reserved instances. When set to false, only include on-demand instances.|
|tag|query|string|false|Filter by device tag|
|type|query|string|false|Filter by instance type (ondemand,spot,reserved)|
|has_termination_time|query|boolean|false|Filter only instances marked for termination. When set to true, only include instances that have a termination time. When set to false, only include instances that do not have a termination time.|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|Page to return|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|Items returned per page|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|categories|compute|
|categories|storage|
|categories|vmce|
|categories|legacy_gen|
|categories|current_gen|

<h3 id="retrieve-all-devices-of-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|ok|[DeviceList](#schemadevicelist)|
|401|Unauthorized|unauthorized|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|not found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve all devices of a project

<a id="opIdfindProjectDevices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/devices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /projects/{id}/devices`

Provides a collection of devices for a given project.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-devices-of-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Project UUID|
|search|query|string|false|Search by hostname, description, short_id, reservation short_id, tags, plan name, plan slug, facility code, facility name, operating system name, operating system slug, IP addresses.|
|categories|query|[[findOrganizationDevices_categories_parameter_inner](#schemafindorganizationdevices_categories_parameter_inner)]|false|Filter by plan category|
|facility|query|string|false|Filter by device facility|
|metro|query|string|false|Filter by device metro|
|hostname|query|string|false|Filter by partial hostname|
|reserved|query|boolean|false|Filter only reserved instances. When set to true, only include reserved instances. When set to false, only include on-demand instances.|
|tag|query|string|false|Filter by device tag|
|type|query|string|false|Filter by instance type (ondemand,spot,reserved)|
|has_termination_time|query|boolean|false|Filter only instances marked for termination. When set to true, only include instances that have a termination time. When set to false, only include instances that do not have a termination time.|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|Page to return|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|Items returned per page|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|categories|compute|
|categories|storage|
|categories|vmce|
|categories|legacy_gen|
|categories|current_gen|

`POST /projects/{id}/devices`

Creates a new device and provisions it in the specified location.

Device type-specific options are accepted.  For example, `baremetal` devices accept `operating_system`, `hostname`, and `plan`. These parameters may not be accepted for other device types. The default device type is `baremetal`.

<h3 id="create-a-device-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Project UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[createDevice_request](#schemacreatedevice_request)|true|Device to create|
|» *oneOf*|body|[DeviceCreateInMetroInput](#schemadevicecreateinmetroinput)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[DeviceCreateInFacilityInput](#schemadevicecreateinfacilityinput)|false|none|

## Move a hardware reservation

<a id="opIdmoveHardwareReservation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/hardware-reservations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/move \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "project_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }'
```

`POST /hardware-reservations/{id}/move`

Move a hardware reservation to another project

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "project_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

<h3 id="move-a-hardware-reservation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Hardware Reservation UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[moveHardwareReservation_request](#schemamovehardwarereservation_request)|true|Destination Project UUID|
|» project_id|body|string(uuid)|false|none|

## Retrieve all hardware reservations for a given project

<a id="opIdfindProjectHardwareReservations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/hardware-reservations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /projects/{id}/hardware-reservations`

Provides a collection of hardware reservations for a given project.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-hardware-reservations-for-a-given-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Project UUID|
|query|query|string|false|Search by facility code, plan name, project name, reservation short ID or device hostname|
|state|query|[findProjectHardwareReservations_state_parameter](#schemafindprojecthardwarereservations_state_parameter)|false|Filter by hardware reservation state|
|provisionable|query|[findProjectHardwareReservations_provisionable_parameter](#schemafindprojecthardwarereservations_provisionable_parameter)|false|Filter hardware reservation that is provisionable|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|Page to return|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|Items returned per page|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|active|
|state|spare|
|state|need_of_service|
|provisionable|only|

## Unassign an ip address

<a id="opIddeleteIPAddress"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/ips/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /ips/{id}`

This call can be used to un-assign an IP assignment or delete
an IP reservation.

Un-assign an IP address record.
Use the assignment UUID you
get after attaching the IP. This will remove the relationship between an IP and the device or metal gateway and will make the IP address available to be assigned to another device, once the IP has been un-configured from the network.

Delete an IP reservation.
Use the reservation UUID you get after adding the IP to the project. This will permanently delete the IP block reservation from the project.


<h3 id="unassign-an-ip-address-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|IP Address UUID|

## Requesting IP reservations

<a id="opIdrequestIPReservation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "comments": "string",
    "customdata": {},
    "details": "string",
    "facility": "string",
    "fail_on_approval_required": true,
    "metro": "SV",
    "quantity": 0,
    "tags": [
      "string"
    ],
    "type": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{id}/ips`

Request more IP space for a project in order to have additional IP addresses to assign to devices.  If the request is within the max quota, an IP reservation will be created. If the project will exceed its IP quota, a request will be submitted for review, and will return an IP Reservation with a `state` of `pending`. You can automatically have the request fail with HTTP status 422 instead of triggering the review process by providing the `fail_on_approval_required` parameter set to `true` in the request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comments": "string",
  "customdata": {},
  "details": "string",
  "facility": "string",
  "fail_on_approval_required": true,
  "metro": "SV",
  "quantity": 0,
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="requesting-ip-reservations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Project UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[requestIPReservation_request](#schemarequestipreservation_request)|true|IP Reservation Request to create|
|» *oneOf*|body|[IPReservationRequestInput](#schemaipreservationrequestinput)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[VrfIpReservationCreateInput](#schemavrfipreservationcreateinput)|false|none|

## Create a Metal Gateway Elastic IP

<a id="opIdcreateMetalGatewayElasticIp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/metal-gateways/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "147.75.234.8/31",
    "next_hop": "192.168.12.13",
    "customdata": {
      "key": ""
    },
    "tags": [
      "NY",
      "prod",
      "public"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /metal-gateways/{id}/ips`

Create a new Elastic IP on this Metal Gateway.

Assign an IPv4 range as an elastic IP to the Metal Gateway, with a specified next-hop address contained within the Metal Gateway.

Notice: Elastic IPs on Metal Gateways are a test feature currently under active development, and only available to certain users. Please contact Customer Success for more information.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "147.75.234.8/31",
  "next_hop": "192.168.12.13",
  "customdata": {
    "key": ""
  },
  "tags": [
    "NY",
    "prod",
    "public"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-metal-gateway-elastic-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Metal Gateway UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[MetalGatewayElasticIpCreateInput](#schemametalgatewayelasticipcreateinput)|true|none|
|» address|body|string|true|An IP address (or IP Address range) contained within one of the project's IP Reservations|
|» next_hop|body|string(ipv4)|true|An IP address contained within the Metal Gateways' IP Reservation range.|
|» customdata|body|object|false|Optional User-defined JSON object value.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Optional list of User-defined tags. Can be used by users to provide additional details or context regarding the purpose or usage of this resource.|

<h1 id="metal-api-organizations">Organizations</h1>

Organizations Management. Check out the product docs to learn more about [Organizations](https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/accounts/).

## Retrieve all organizations

<a id="opIdfindOrganizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/organizations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /organizations`

Returns a list of organizations that are accessible to the current user.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-organizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|personal|query|[findOrganizations_personal_parameter](#schemafindorganizations_personal_parameter)|false|Include, exclude or show only personal organizations.|
|without_projects|query|[findOrganizations_personal_parameter](#schemafindorganizations_personal_parameter)|false|Include, exclude or show only organizations that have no projects.|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|Page to return|
|per_page|query|integer(int32)|false|Items returned per page|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|personal|include|
|personal|exclude|
|personal|only|
|without_projects|include|
|without_projects|exclude|
|without_projects|only|

## Create an invitation for an organization

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationInvitation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/organizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/invitations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "projects_ids": [
      "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
      "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91"
    ],
    "organization_id": "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
    "roles": [
      null,
      null
    ],
    "message": "message",
    "invitee": "invitee"
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{id}/invitations`

In order to add a user to an organization, they must first be invited.
To invite to several projects the parameter `projects_ids:[a,b,c]` can be used

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "projects_ids": [
    "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
    "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91"
  ],
  "organization_id": "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
  "roles": [
    null,
    null
  ],
  "message": "message",
  "invitee": "invitee"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-invitation-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Organization UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[InvitationInput](#schemainvitationinput)|true|Invitation to create|
|» invitee|body|string(email)|true|none|
|» message|body|string|false|none|

`POST /organizations/{id}/projects`

Creates a new project for the organization

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "payment_method_id": "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
```

<h3 id="create-a-project-for-the-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Organization UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[ProjectCreateInput](#schemaprojectcreateinput)|true|Project to create|
|» customdata|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the project. Cannot contain characters encoded in greater than 3 bytes such as emojis.|
|» payment_method_id|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» type|body|[ProjectCreateFromRootInput_type](#schemaprojectcreatefromrootinput_type)|false|The type of the project. If no type is specified the project type will automatically be `default` Projects of type 'vmce' are part of an in development feature and not available to all customers.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|none|

|Parameter|Value|

<a id="opIdcreatePortVlanAssignmentBatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/ports/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/vlan-assignments/batches \

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "vlan_assignments": [

        "native": true,
        "state": null
      },
      {
        "vlan": "vlan",
        "native": true,
        "state": null
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /ports/{id}/vlan-assignments/batches`

## Retrieve a VLAN Assignment Batch's details

<a id="opIdfindPortVlanAssignmentBatchByPortIdAndBatchId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/ports/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/vlan-assignments/batches/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /ports/{id}/vlan-assignments/batches/{batch_id}`

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Port UUID|
|batch_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Batch ID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|

## Create a project

<a id="opIdcreateProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "payment_method_id": "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
    "organization_id": "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
    "name": "name",
    "customdata": "{}",
    "type": null,
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /projects`

Creates a new project for the user default organization. If the user don't have an organization, a new one will be created.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "payment_method_id": "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
  "organization_id": "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
  "name": "name",
  "customdata": "{}",
  "type": null,
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[ProjectCreateFromRootInput](#schemaprojectcreatefromrootinput)|true|Project to create|
|» customdata|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the project. Cannot contain characters encoded in greater than 3 bytes such as emojis.|
|» organization_id|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» payment_method_id|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» type|body|[ProjectCreateFromRootInput_type](#schemaprojectcreatefromrootinput_type)|false|The type of the project. If no type is specified the project type will automatically be `default` Projects of type 'vmce' are part of an in development feature and not available to all customers.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|default|
|» type|vmce|

## Get spot market prices for a given period of time

<a id="opIdfindSpotMarketPricesHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/market/spot/prices/history?facility=string&plan=string&from=string&until=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /market/spot/prices/history`

Get spot market prices for a given plan and facility in a fixed period of time

*Note: In the `200` response, the property `datapoints` contains arrays of `[float, integer]`.*

<h3 id="get-spot-market-prices-for-a-given-period-of-time-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|facility|query|string|true|Facility to check spot market prices|
|plan|query|string|true|Plan to check spot market prices|
|metro|query|string|false|Metro to check spot market price history|
|from|query|string|true|Timestamp from range|
|until|query|string|true|Timestamp to range|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "prices_history": {
    "datapoints": [
      null,
      null
    ]
  }
}
```

```json
    "string"
  ]
```

```json
  ]
```

## Create a spot market request

<a id="opIdcreateSpotMarketRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/spot-market-requests \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "end_at": "2000-01-23T04:56:07.000+00:00",
    "instance_parameters": {
      "user_ssh_keys": [
        "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
        "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91"
      ],
      "private_ipv4_subnet_size": 1,
      "description": "description",
      "hostnames": [
        "hostnames",
        "hostnames"
      ],
      "termination_time": "2000-01-23T04:56:07.000+00:00",
      "project_ssh_keys": [
        "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
        "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91"
      ],
      "tags": [
        "tags",
        "tags"
      ],
      "features": [
        "features",
        "features"
      ],
      "userdata": "userdata",
      "hostname": "hostname",
      "no_ssh_keys": true,
      "public_ipv4_subnet_size": 5,
      "operating_system": "operating_system",
      "always_pxe": true,
      "billing_cycle": "billing_cycle",
      "customdata": "{}",
      "locked": true,
      "plan": "plan"
    },
    "metro": "metro",
    "devices_min": 6,
    "devices_max": 0,
    "max_bid_price": 5.637377,
    "facilities": [
      "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
      "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{id}/spot-market-requests`

Creates a new spot market request.

Type-specific options (such as operating_system for baremetal devices) should be included in the main data structure alongside hostname and plan.

The features attribute allows you to optionally specify what features your server should have. For example, if you require a server with a TPM chip, you may specify `{ "features": { "tpm": "required" } }` (or `{ "features": ["tpm"] }` in shorthand).

The request will fail if there are no available servers matching your criteria. Alternatively, if you do not require a certain feature, but would prefer to be assigned a server with that feature if there are any available, you may specify that feature with a preferred value (see the example request below).

The request will not fail if we have no servers with that feature in our inventory.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "end_at": "2000-01-23T04:56:07.000+00:00",
  "instance_parameters": {
    "user_ssh_keys": [
      "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
      "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91"
    ],
    "private_ipv4_subnet_size": 1,
    "description": "description",
    "hostnames": [
      "hostnames",
      "hostnames"
    ],
    "termination_time": "2000-01-23T04:56:07.000+00:00",
    "project_ssh_keys": [
      "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
      "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91"
    ],
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ],
    "features": [
      "features",
      "features"
    ],
    "userdata": "userdata",
    "hostname": "hostname",
    "no_ssh_keys": true,
    "public_ipv4_subnet_size": 5,
    "operating_system": "operating_system",
    "always_pxe": true,
    "billing_cycle": "billing_cycle",
    "customdata": "{}",
    "locked": true,
    "plan": "plan"
  },
  "metro": "metro",
  "devices_min": 6,
  "devices_max": 0,
  "max_bid_price": 5.637377,
  "facilities": [
    "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
    "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-spot-market-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Project UUID|
|body|body|[SpotMarketRequestCreateInput](#schemaspotmarketrequestcreateinput)|true|Spot Market Request to create|
|» devices_max|body|integer|false|none|
|» devices_min|body|integer|false|none|
|» end_at|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» facilities|body|[string(uuid)]|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» instance_parameters|body|[SpotMarketRequestCreateInput_instance_parameters](#schemaspotmarketrequestcreateinput_instance_parameters)|false|none|
|» max_bid_price|body|number(float)|false|none|
|» metro|body|string|false|The metro ID or code the spot market request will be created in.|

## Create a virtual network

<a id="opIdcreateVirtualNetwork"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/virtual-networks \
  -X POST \

  -d '{

      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{id}/virtual-networks`

Creates an virtual network.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "vxlan": 1099,
  "metro": "metro",
  "description": "description",
  "facility": "facility",
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-virtual-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Project UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[VirtualNetworkCreateInput](#schemavirtualnetworkcreateinput)|true|Virtual Network to create|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» facility|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** The UUID (or facility code) for the Facility in which to create this Virtual network.|
|» metro|body|string|false|The UUID (or metro code) for the Metro in which to create this Virtual Network.|
|» vxlan|body|integer|false|VLAN ID between 2-3999. Must be unique for the project within the Metro in which this Virtual Network is being created. If no value is specified, the next-available VLAN ID in the range 1000-1999 will be automatically selected.|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```


`DELETE /virtual-networks/{id}`

Deletes a virtual network.

<h3 id="delete-a-virtual-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Virtual Network UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|

<h1 id="metal-api-vrfs">VRFs</h1>

VRF Management. A VRF is a project-scoped virtual router resource that defines a collection of customer-managed IP blocks that can be used in BGP peering on one or more virtual networks. Metal Gateways and Interconnection Virtual Circuits can take advantage of VRFs to enable Layer 3 routing with bespoke network ranges. Notice: VRFs are a test feature currently under active development, and only available to certain users. Please contact Customer Success for more information.


## Retrieve a BGP Dynamic Neighbor

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/bgp-dynamic-neighbors/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /bgp-dynamic-neighbors/{id}`

Return a single BGP Dynamic Neighbor resource

<h3 id="retrieve-a-bgp-dynamic-neighbor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|404|Not Found|Not Found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Delete a VRF BGP Dynamic Neighbor

<a id="opIddeleteBgpDynamicNeighborById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/bgp-dynamic-neighbors/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /bgp-dynamic-neighbors/{id}`

Trigger the removal of a BGP Neighbor range from a VRF

<h3 id="delete-a-vrf-bgp-dynamic-neighbor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|BGP Dynamic Neighbor UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|

<h3 id="delete-a-vrf-bgp-dynamic-neighbor-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|[BgpDynamicNeighbor](#schemabgpdynamicneighbor)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## List BGP Dynamic Neighbors

<a id="opIdgetBgpDynamicNeighbors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/metal-gateways/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/bgp-dynamic-neighbors \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /metal-gateways/{id}/bgp-dynamic-neighbors`

Returns the list of VRF BGP Dynamic Neighbors for this Metal Gateway

<h3 id="list-bgp-dynamic-neighbors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Metal Gateway UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|

## Create a VRF BGP Dynamic Neighbor range

<a id="opIdcreateBgpDynamicNeighbor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/metal-gateways/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/bgp-dynamic-neighbors \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "bgp_neighbor_asn": 12345,
    "bgp_neighbor_range": "192.168.1.0/25",
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /metal-gateways/{id}/bgp-dynamic-neighbors`

Create a VRF BGP Dynamic Neighbor range.

BGP Dynamic Neighbor records are limited to 2 per Virtual Network.

Notice: VRFs are a test feature currently under active development, and only available to certain users. Please contact Customer Success for more information.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bgp_neighbor_asn": 12345,
  "bgp_neighbor_range": "192.168.1.0/25",
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-vrf-bgp-dynamic-neighbor-range-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Metal Gateway UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[BgpDynamicNeighborCreateInput](#schemabgpdynamicneighborcreateinput)|true|none|
|» bgp_neighbor_range|body|string|true|Network range of the dynamic BGP neighbor in CIDR format|
|» bgp_neighbor_asn|body|integer|true|The ASN of the dynamic BGP neighbor|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|none|

<h3 id="create-a-vrf-bgp-dynamic-neighbor-range-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[BgpDynamicNeighbor](#schemabgpdynamicneighbor)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve all VRFs in the project

<a id="opIdfindVrfs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/vrfs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /projects/{id}/vrfs`

Returns the list of VRFs for a single project.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-vrfs-in-the-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Project UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|metro|query|string|false|Filter by Metro ID (uuid) or Metro Code|

## Create a new VRF in the specified project

<a id="opIdcreateVrf"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/projects/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/vrfs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_export_route_map": true,
    "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_bfd_enabled": true,
    "ip_ranges": [
      "ip_ranges",
      "ip_ranges"
    ],
    "local_asn": 0,
    "metro": "metro",
    "name": "name",
    "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_enabled": true,
    "description": "description",
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{id}/vrfs`

Creates a new VRF in the specified project

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_export_route_map": true,
  "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_bfd_enabled": true,
  "ip_ranges": [
    "ip_ranges",
    "ip_ranges"
  ],
  "local_asn": 0,
  "metro": "metro",
  "name": "name",
  "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_enabled": true,
  "description": "description",
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-vrf-in-the-specified-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Project UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[VrfCreateInput](#schemavrfcreateinput)|true|VRF to create|
|» bgp_dynamic_neighbors_enabled|body|boolean|false|Toggle to enable the dynamic bgp neighbors feature on the VRF|
|» bgp_dynamic_neighbors_export_route_map|body|boolean|false|Toggle to export the VRF route-map to the dynamic bgp neighbors|
|» bgp_dynamic_neighbors_bfd_enabled|body|boolean|false|Toggle BFD on dynamic bgp neighbors sessions|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» ip_ranges|body|[string]|false|A list of CIDR network addresses. Like ["10.0.0.0/16", "2001:d78::/56"]. IPv4 blocks must be between /8 and /29 in size. IPv6 blocks must be between /56 and /64. A VRF\'s IP ranges must be defined in order to create VRF IP Reservations, which can then be used for Metal Gateways or Virtual Circuits.|
|» local_asn|body|integer(int32)|false|none|
|» metro|body|string|true|The UUID (or metro code) for the Metro in which to create this VRF.|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|none|

<h3 id="retrieve-a-vrf-route-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[VrfRoute](#schemavrfroute)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Update a VRF Route

<a id="opIdupdateVrfRouteById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/routes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "prefix": "0.0.0.0/0",
    "next_hop": "192.168.1.254",
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /routes/{id}`

Requests a VRF Route be redeployed across the network. Updating the prefix or next-hop address on a route is not currently supported.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "prefix": "0.0.0.0/0",
  "next_hop": "192.168.1.254",
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-vrf-route-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|VRF Route UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[VrfRouteUpdateInput](#schemavrfrouteupdateinput)|true|none|
|» prefix|body|string|false|The IPv4 prefix for the route, in CIDR-style notation. For a static default route, this will always be "0.0.0.0/0"|
|» next_hop|body|string(ipv4)|false|The IPv4 address within the VRF of the host that will handle this route|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|none|

<h3 id="update-a-vrf-route-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|[VrfRoute](#schemavrfroute)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable Entity|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too Many Requests|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Delete a VRF Route

<a id="opIddeleteVrfRouteById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/routes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /routes/{id}`

Trigger the deletion of a VRF Route resource. The status of the route will update to 'deleting', and the route resource will remain accessible while background operations remove the route from the network. Once the route has been removed from the network, the resource will be fully deleted.

<h3 id="delete-a-vrf-route-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|VRF Route UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|

## Retrieve a VRF

<a id="opIdfindVrfById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/vrfs/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /vrfs/{id}`

Returns a single VRF resource

<h3 id="retrieve-a-vrf-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|VRF UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|

## Update the VRF

<a id="opIdupdateVrf"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/vrfs/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_export_route_map": true,
    "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_bfd_enabled": true,
    "ip_ranges": [
      "ip_ranges",
      "ip_ranges"
    ],
    "local_asn": 0,
    "name": "name",
    "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_enabled": true,
    "description": "description",
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /vrfs/{id}`

Updates the VRF.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_export_route_map": true,
  "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_bfd_enabled": true,
  "ip_ranges": [
    "ip_ranges",
    "ip_ranges"
  ],
  "local_asn": 0,
  "name": "name",
  "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_enabled": true,
  "description": "description",
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-vrf-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|VRF UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[VrfUpdateInput](#schemavrfupdateinput)|true|VRF to update|
|» bgp_dynamic_neighbors_enabled|body|boolean|false|Toggle to enable the dynamic bgp neighbors feature on the VRF|
|» bgp_dynamic_neighbors_export_route_map|body|boolean|false|Toggle to export the VRF route-map to the dynamic bgp neighbors|
|» bgp_dynamic_neighbors_bfd_enabled|body|boolean|false|Toggle BFD on dynamic bgp neighbors sessions|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» ip_ranges|body|[string]|false|A list of CIDR network addresses. Like ["10.0.0.0/16", "2001:d78::/56"]. IPv4 blocks must be between /8 and /29 in size. IPv6 blocks must be between /56 and /64. A VRF\'s IP ranges must be defined in order to create VRF IP Reservations, which can then be used for Metal Gateways or Virtual Circuits. Adding a new CIDR address to the list will result in the creation of a new IP Range for this VRF. Removal of an existing CIDR address from the list will result in the deletion of an existing IP Range for this VRF. Deleting an IP Range will result in the deletion of any VRF IP Reservations contained within the IP Range, as well as the VRF IP Reservation\'s associated Metal Gateways or Virtual Circuits. If you do not wish to add or remove IP Ranges, either include the full existing list of IP Ranges in the update request, or do not specify the `ip_ranges` field in the update request. Specifying a value of `[]` will remove all existing IP Ranges from the VRF.|
|» local_asn|body|integer(int32)|false|The new `local_asn` value for the VRF. This field cannot be updated when there are active Interconnection Virtual Circuits associated to the VRF, or if any of the VLANs of the VRF's metal gateway has been assigned on an instance.|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|none|

## Delete the VRF

<a id="opIddeleteVrf"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/vrfs/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /vrfs/{id}`

Deletes the VRF

<h3 id="delete-the-vrf-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|VRF UUID|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "errors": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "errors": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "errors": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-the-vrf-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|no content|None|
|401|Unauthorized|unauthorized|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|not found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve all VRF IP Reservations in the VRF

<a id="opIdfindVrfIpReservations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/vrfs/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/ips \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /vrfs/{id}/ips`

Returns the list of VRF IP Reservations for the VRF.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-vrf-ip-reservations-in-the-vrf-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|VRF UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply nested objects.|

<h3 id="retrieve-all-vrf-ip-reservations-in-the-vrf-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|ok|[VrfIpReservationList](#schemavrfipreservationlist)|
|403|Forbidden|forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|not found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve all VRF IP Reservations in the VRF

<a id="opIdfindVrfIpReservation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/vrfs/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/ips/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /vrfs/{vrf_id}/ips/{id}`

Returns the IP Reservation for the VRF.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-vrf-ip-reservations-in-the-vrf-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|vrf_id|path|string(uuid)|true|VRF UUID|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|IP UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply nested objects.|

<h3 id="retrieve-all-vrf-ip-reservations-in-the-vrf-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|ok|[VrfIpReservation](#schemavrfipreservation)|
|403|Forbidden|forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|not found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve all routes in the VRF

<a id="opIdgetVrfRoutes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/vrfs/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/routes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /vrfs/{id}/routes`

Returns the list of routes for the VRF

<h3 id="retrieve-all-routes-in-the-vrf-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|VRF UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|

<h3 id="retrieve-all-routes-in-the-vrf-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[VrfRouteList](#schemavrfroutelist)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
x_auth_token
</aside>

## Create a VRF route

<a id="opIdcreateVrfRoute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.equinix.com/metal/v1/vrfs/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/routes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "prefix": "0.0.0.0/0",
    "next_hop": "192.168.1.254",
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /vrfs/{id}/routes`

Create a route in a VRF. Currently only static default routes are supported.

Notice: VRFs are a test feature currently under active development, and only available to certain users. Please contact Customer Success for more information.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "prefix": "0.0.0.0/0",
  "next_hop": "192.168.1.254",
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-vrf-route-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|VRF UUID|
|include|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to include. Included objects will return their full<br>attributes. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to included deeply<br>nested objects.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Nested attributes to exclude. Excluded objects will return only the href<br>attribute. Attribute names can be dotted (up to 3 levels) to exclude deeply<br>nested objects.|
|body|body|[VrfRouteCreateInput](#schemavrfroutecreateinput)|true|none|
|» prefix|body|string|true|The IPv4 prefix for the route, in CIDR-style notation. For a static default route, this will always be "0.0.0.0/0"|
|» next_hop|body|string(ipv4)|true|The IPv4 address within the VRF of the host that will handle this route|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|none|

## Retrieve all invoices for an organization

|status|query|string|false|filter by status|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|asn|integer(int32)|false|none|Autonomous System Number. ASN is required with Global BGP. With Local BGP the private ASN, 65000, is assigned.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|deployment_type|[BgpConfig_deployment_type](#schemabgpconfig_deployment_type)|false|none|In a Local BGP deployment, a customer uses an internal ASN to control routes within a single Equinix Metal datacenter. This means that the routes are never advertised to the global Internet. Global BGP, on the other hand, requires a customer to have a registered ASN and IP space.<br>|
|href|string|false|none|none|
|id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|max_prefix|integer|false|none|The maximum number of route filters allowed per server|
|md5|string \| null|false|none|(Optional) Password for BGP session in plaintext (not a checksum)|
|project|[Href](#schemahref)|false|none|none|
|ranges|[[GlobalBgpRange](#schemaglobalbgprange)]|false|none|The IP block ranges associated to the ASN (Populated in Global BGP only)|
|requested_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|route_object|string|false|none|Specifies AS-MACRO (aka AS-SET) to use when building client route filters|
|sessions|[[BgpSession](#schemabgpsession)]|false|none|The direct connections between neighboring routers that want to exchange routing information.|
|status|[BgpConfig_status](#schemabgpconfig_status)|false|none|Status of the BGP Config. Status "requested" is valid only with the "global" deployment_type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|deployment_type|global|
|deployment_type|local|
|status|requested|
|status|enabled|
|status|disabled|

```json
  "use_case": "use_case",
  "deployment_type": "local",
  "asn": 65000,
  "md5": "md5"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|asn|integer|true|none|Autonomous System Number for local BGP deployment.|
|deployment_type|[BgpConfigRequestInput_deployment_type](#schemabgpconfigrequestinput_deployment_type)|true|none|Wether the BGP deployment is local or global. Local deployments are configured immediately. Global deployments will need to be reviewed by Equinix Metal engineers.|
|md5|string|false|none|The plaintext password to share between BGP neighbors as an MD5 checksum:<br>* must be 10-20 characters long<br>* may not include punctuation<br>* must be a combination of numbers and letters<br>* must contain at least one lowercase, uppercase, and digit character<br>|
|use_case|string|false|none|A use case explanation (necessary for global BGP request review).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|deployment_type|local|
|deployment_type|global|

|multihop|boolean|false|none|True when the BGP session should be configured as multihop.|
|peer_as|integer(int32)|false|none|The Peer ASN to use when configuring BGP on your device.|
|peer_ips|[string]|false|none|A list of one or more IP addresses to use for the Peer IP section of your BGP configuration. For non-multihop sessions, this will typically be a single gateway address for the device. For multihop sessions, it will be a list of IPs.|

|routes_out|[[BgpRoute](#schemabgproute)]|false|none|A list of outgoing routes. Only populated if the BGP session has default route enabled.|

|state|[Device_state](#schemadevice_state)|false|none|The current state the instance is in.<br><br>* When an instance is initially created it will be in the `queued` state until it is picked up by the provisioner.<br>* Once provisioning has begun on the instance it's state will move to `provisioning`.<br>* When an instance is deleted, it will move to `deprovisioning` state until the deprovision is completed and the instance state moves to `deleted`.<br>* If an instance fails to provision or deprovision it will move to `failed` state.<br>* Once an instance has completed provisioning it will move to `active` state.<br>* If an instance is currently powering off or powering on it will move to `powering_off` or `powering_on` states respectively. <br>* When the instance is powered off completely it will move to the `inactive` state.<br>* When an instance is powered on completely it will move to the `active` state.<br>* Using the reinstall action to install a new OS on the instance will cause the instance state to change to `reinstalling`.<br>* When the reinstall action is complete the instance will move to `active` state.|
|storage|[Storage](#schemastorage)|false|none|none|
|switch_uuid|string|false|none|Switch short id. This can be used to determine if two devices are<br>connected to the same switch, for example.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|
|termination_time|string(date-time)|false|none|When the device will be terminated. If you don't supply timezone info, the timestamp is assumed to be in UTC.<br><br>This is commonly set in advance for<br>ephemeral spot market instances but this field may also be set with<br>on-demand and reservation instances to automatically delete the resource<br>at a given time. The termination time can also be used to release a<br>hardware reservation instance at a given time, keeping the reservation<br>open for other uses.  On a spot market device, the termination time will<br>be set automatically when outbid.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|user|string|false|none|none|
|userdata|string|false|none|none|
|volumes|[[Href](#schemahref)]|false|none|none|
|sos|string|false|none|Hostname used to connect to the instance via the SOS (Serial over SSH) out-of-band console.|

|state|powering_off|
