### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|always_pxe|boolean|false|none|When true, devices with a `custom_ipxe` OS will always boot to iPXE. The<br>default setting of false ensures that iPXE will be used on only the<br>first boot.|
|billing_cycle|[DeviceCreateInput_billing_cycle](#schemadevicecreateinput_billing_cycle)|false|none|The billing cycle of the device.|
|customdata|object|false|none|Customdata is an arbitrary JSON value that can be accessed via the<br>metadata service.|
|description|string|false|none|Any description of the device or how it will be used. This may be used<br>to inform other API consumers with project access.|
|features|[string]|false|none|The features attribute allows you to optionally specify what features your server should have.<br><br>In the API shorthand syntax, all features listed are `required`:<br><br>```<br>{ "features": ["tpm"] }<br>```<br><br>Alternatively, if you do not require a certain feature, but would prefer to be assigned a server with that feature if there are any available, you may specify that feature with a `preferred` value. The request will not fail if we have no servers with that feature in our inventory. The API offers an alternative syntax for mixing preferred and required features:<br><br>```<br>{ "features": { "tpm": "required", "raid": "preferred" } }<br>```<br><br>The request will only fail if there are no available servers matching the required `tpm` criteria.|
|hardware_reservation_id|string|false|none|The Hardware Reservation UUID to provision. Alternatively, `next-available` can be specified to select from any of the available hardware reservations. An error will be returned if the requested reservation option is not available.<br><br>See [Reserved Hardware](https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/deploy/reserved/) for more details.|
|hostname|string|false|none|The hostname to use within the operating system. The same hostname may be used on multiple devices within a project.|
|ip_addresses|[[IPAddress](#schemaipaddress)]|false|none|The `ip_addresses attribute will allow you to specify the addresses you want created with your device.<br><br>The default value configures public IPv4, public IPv6, and private IPv4.<br><br>Private IPv4 address is required. When specifying `ip_addresses`, one of the array items must enable private IPv4.<br><br>Some operating systems require public IPv4 address. In those cases you will receive an error message if public IPv4 is not enabled.<br><br>For example, to only configure your server with a private IPv4 address, you can send `{ "ip_addresses": [{ "address_family": 4, "public": false }] }`.<br><br>It is possible to request a subnet size larger than a `/30` by assigning addresses using the UUID(s) of ip_reservations in your project.<br><br>For example, `{ "ip_addresses": [..., {"address_family": 4, "public": true, "ip_reservations": ["uuid1", "uuid2"]}] }`<br><br>To access a server without public IPs, you can use our Out-of-Band console access (SOS) or proxy through another server in the project with public IPs enabled.|
|ipxe_script_url|string|false|none|When set, the device will chainload an iPXE Script at boot fetched from the supplied URL.<br><br>See [Custom iPXE](https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/operating-systems/custom-ipxe/) for more details.|
|locked|boolean|false|none|Whether the device should be locked, preventing accidental deletion.|
|network_frozen|boolean|false|none|If true, this instance can not be converted to a different network type.|
|no_ssh_keys|boolean|false|none|Overrides default behaviour of attaching all of the organization members ssh keys and project ssh keys to device if no specific keys specified|
|operating_system|string|true|none|The slug of the operating system to provision. Check the Equinix Metal operating system documentation for rules that may be imposed per operating system, including restrictions on IP address options and device plans.|
|plan|string|true|none|The slug of the device plan to provision.|
|private_ipv4_subnet_size|integer(int32)|false|none|Deprecated. Use ip_addresses. Subnet range for addresses allocated to this device.|
|project_ssh_keys|[string(uuid)]|false|none|A list of UUIDs identifying the device parent project<br>that should be authorized to access this device (typically<br>via /root/.ssh/authorized_keys). These keys will also appear in the device metadata.<br><br>If no SSH keys are specified (`user_ssh_keys`, `project_ssh_keys`, and `ssh_keys` are all empty lists or omitted),<br>all parent project keys, parent project members keys and organization members keys will be included. This behaviour can<br>be changed with 'no_ssh_keys' option to omit any SSH key being added.<br>|
|public_ipv4_subnet_size|integer(int32)|false|none|Deprecated. Use ip_addresses. Subnet range for addresses allocated to this device. Your project must have addresses available for a non-default request.|
|spot_instance|boolean|false|none|Create a spot instance. Spot instances are created with a maximum bid price. If the bid price is not met, the spot instance will be terminated as indicated by the `termination_time` field.|
|spot_price_max|number(float)|false|none|The maximum amount to bid for a spot instance.|
|ssh_keys|[[SSHKeyInput](#schemasshkeyinput)]|false|none|A list of new or existing project ssh_keys<br>that should be authorized to access this device (typically<br>via /root/.ssh/authorized_keys). These keys will also<br>appear in the device metadata.<br><br>These keys are added in addition to any keys defined by<br>  `project_ssh_keys` and `user_ssh_keys`.<br>|
|storage|[Storage](#schemastorage)|false|none|none|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|
|termination_time|string(date-time)|false|none|When the device will be terminated. If you don't supply timezone info, the timestamp is assumed to be in UTC.<br><br>This is commonly set in advance for<br>ephemeral spot market instances but this field may also be set with<br>on-demand and reservation instances to automatically delete the resource<br>at a given time. The termination time can also be used to release a<br>hardware reservation instance at a given time, keeping the reservation<br>open for other uses.  On a spot market device, the termination time will<br>be set automatically when outbid.<br>|
|user_ssh_keys|[string(uuid)]|false|none|A list of UUIDs identifying the users<br>that should be authorized to access this device (typically<br>via /root/.ssh/authorized_keys).  These keys will also<br>appear in the device metadata.<br><br>The users must be members of the project or organization.<br><br>If no SSH keys are specified (`user_ssh_keys`, `project_ssh_keys`, and `ssh_keys` are all empty lists or omitted),<br>all parent project keys, parent project members keys and organization members keys will be included. This behaviour can<br>be changed with 'no_ssh_keys' option to omit any SSH key being added.<br>|
|userdata|string|false|none|The userdata presented in the metadata service for this device.  Userdata is fetched and interpreted by the operating system installed on the device. Acceptable formats are determined by the operating system, with the exception of a special iPXE enabling syntax which is handled before the operating system starts.<br><br>See [Server User Data](https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/servers/user-data/) and [Provisioning with Custom iPXE](https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/operating-systems/custom-ipxe/#provisioning-with-custom-ipxe) for more details.|

|billing_cycle|daily|
|billing_cycle|monthly|
|billing_cycle|yearly|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metro|string|true|none|Metro code or ID of where the instance should be provisioned in.<br>Either metro or facility must be provided.|
|always_pxe|boolean|false|none|When true, devices with a `custom_ipxe` OS will always boot to iPXE. The<br>default setting of false ensures that iPXE will be used on only the<br>first boot.|
|billing_cycle|[DeviceCreateInput_billing_cycle](#schemadevicecreateinput_billing_cycle)|false|none|The billing cycle of the device.|
|customdata|object|false|none|Customdata is an arbitrary JSON value that can be accessed via the<br>metadata service.|
|description|string|false|none|Any description of the device or how it will be used. This may be used<br>to inform other API consumers with project access.|
|features|[string]|false|none|The features attribute allows you to optionally specify what features your server should have.<br><br>In the API shorthand syntax, all features listed are `required`:<br><br>```<br>{ "features": ["tpm"] }<br>```<br><br>Alternatively, if you do not require a certain feature, but would prefer to be assigned a server with that feature if there are any available, you may specify that feature with a `preferred` value. The request will not fail if we have no servers with that feature in our inventory. The API offers an alternative syntax for mixing preferred and required features:<br><br>```<br>{ "features": { "tpm": "required", "raid": "preferred" } }<br>```<br><br>The request will only fail if there are no available servers matching the required `tpm` criteria.|
|hardware_reservation_id|string|false|none|The Hardware Reservation UUID to provision. Alternatively, `next-available` can be specified to select from any of the available hardware reservations. An error will be returned if the requested reservation option is not available.<br><br>See [Reserved Hardware](https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/deploy/reserved/) for more details.|
|hostname|string|false|none|The hostname to use within the operating system. The same hostname may be used on multiple devices within a project.|
|ip_addresses|[[IPAddress](#schemaipaddress)]|false|none|The `ip_addresses attribute will allow you to specify the addresses you want created with your device.<br><br>The default value configures public IPv4, public IPv6, and private IPv4.<br><br>Private IPv4 address is required. When specifying `ip_addresses`, one of the array items must enable private IPv4.<br><br>Some operating systems require public IPv4 address. In those cases you will receive an error message if public IPv4 is not enabled.<br><br>For example, to only configure your server with a private IPv4 address, you can send `{ "ip_addresses": [{ "address_family": 4, "public": false }] }`.<br><br>It is possible to request a subnet size larger than a `/30` by assigning addresses using the UUID(s) of ip_reservations in your project.<br><br>For example, `{ "ip_addresses": [..., {"address_family": 4, "public": true, "ip_reservations": ["uuid1", "uuid2"]}] }`<br><br>To access a server without public IPs, you can use our Out-of-Band console access (SOS) or proxy through another server in the project with public IPs enabled.|
|ipxe_script_url|string|false|none|When set, the device will chainload an iPXE Script at boot fetched from the supplied URL.<br><br>See [Custom iPXE](https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/operating-systems/custom-ipxe/) for more details.|
|locked|boolean|false|none|Whether the device should be locked, preventing accidental deletion.|
|network_frozen|boolean|false|none|If true, this instance can not be converted to a different network type.|
|no_ssh_keys|boolean|false|none|Overrides default behaviour of attaching all of the organization members ssh keys and project ssh keys to device if no specific keys specified|
|operating_system|string|true|none|The slug of the operating system to provision. Check the Equinix Metal operating system documentation for rules that may be imposed per operating system, including restrictions on IP address options and device plans.|
|plan|string|true|none|The slug of the device plan to provision.|
|private_ipv4_subnet_size|integer(int32)|false|none|Deprecated. Use ip_addresses. Subnet range for addresses allocated to this device.|
|project_ssh_keys|[string(uuid)]|false|none|A list of UUIDs identifying the device parent project<br>that should be authorized to access this device (typically<br>via /root/.ssh/authorized_keys). These keys will also appear in the device metadata.<br><br>If no SSH keys are specified (`user_ssh_keys`, `project_ssh_keys`, and `ssh_keys` are all empty lists or omitted),<br>all parent project keys, parent project members keys and organization members keys will be included. This behaviour can<br>be changed with 'no_ssh_keys' option to omit any SSH key being added.<br>|
|public_ipv4_subnet_size|integer(int32)|false|none|Deprecated. Use ip_addresses. Subnet range for addresses allocated to this device. Your project must have addresses available for a non-default request.|
|spot_instance|boolean|false|none|Create a spot instance. Spot instances are created with a maximum bid price. If the bid price is not met, the spot instance will be terminated as indicated by the `termination_time` field.|
|spot_price_max|number(float)|false|none|The maximum amount to bid for a spot instance.|
|ssh_keys|[[SSHKeyInput](#schemasshkeyinput)]|false|none|A list of new or existing project ssh_keys<br>that should be authorized to access this device (typically<br>via /root/.ssh/authorized_keys). These keys will also<br>appear in the device metadata.<br><br>These keys are added in addition to any keys defined by<br>  `project_ssh_keys` and `user_ssh_keys`.<br>|
|storage|[Storage](#schemastorage)|false|none|none|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|
|termination_time|string(date-time)|false|none|When the device will be terminated. If you don't supply timezone info, the timestamp is assumed to be in UTC.<br><br>This is commonly set in advance for<br>ephemeral spot market instances but this field may also be set with<br>on-demand and reservation instances to automatically delete the resource<br>at a given time. The termination time can also be used to release a<br>hardware reservation instance at a given time, keeping the reservation<br>open for other uses.  On a spot market device, the termination time will<br>be set automatically when outbid.<br>|
|user_ssh_keys|[string(uuid)]|false|none|A list of UUIDs identifying the users<br>that should be authorized to access this device (typically<br>via /root/.ssh/authorized_keys).  These keys will also<br>appear in the device metadata.<br><br>The users must be members of the project or organization.<br><br>If no SSH keys are specified (`user_ssh_keys`, `project_ssh_keys`, and `ssh_keys` are all empty lists or omitted),<br>all parent project keys, parent project members keys and organization members keys will be included. This behaviour can<br>be changed with 'no_ssh_keys' option to omit any SSH key being added.<br>|
|userdata|string|false|none|The userdata presented in the metadata service for this device.  Userdata is fetched and interpreted by the operating system installed on the device. Acceptable formats are determined by the operating system, with the exception of a special iPXE enabling syntax which is handled before the operating system starts.<br><br>See [Server User Data](https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/servers/user-data/) and [Provisioning with Custom iPXE](https://metal.equinix.com/developers/docs/operating-systems/custom-ipxe/#provisioning-with-custom-ipxe) for more details.|

<h2 id="tocS_FabricServiceToken">FabricServiceToken</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafabricservicetoken"></a>
<a id="schema_FabricServiceToken"></a>
<a id="tocSfabricservicetoken"></a>
<a id="tocsfabricservicetoken"></a>

```json
{
  "max_allowed_speed": 10000000000,
  "expires_at": "2000-01-23T04:56:07.000+00:00",
  "role": null,
  "service_token_type": null,
  "id": "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
  "state": null
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expires_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The expiration date and time of the Fabric service token. Once a service token is expired, it is no longer redeemable.|
|id|string(uuid)|false|none|The UUID that can be used on the Fabric Portal to redeem either an A-Side or Z-Side Service Token.<br>For Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), this UUID will represent an A-Side Service Token, which will allow interconnections<br>to be made from Equinix Metal to other Service Providers on Fabric. For Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed), this UUID will<br>represent a Z-Side Service Token, which will allow interconnections to be made to connect an owned Fabric Port or <br>Virtual Device to Equinix Metal.|
|max_allowed_speed|integer|false|none|The maximum speed that can be selected on the Fabric Portal when configuring a interconnection with either <br>an A-Side or Z-Side Service Token. For Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), this is what the billing is based off of, and can be one<br>of the following options, '50mbps', '200mbps', '500mbps', '1gbps', '2gbps', '5gbps' or '10gbps'. For Fabric VCs<br>(Fabric Billed), this will default to 10Gbps.|
|role|[FabricServiceToken_role](#schemafabricservicetoken_role)|false|none|Either primary or secondary, depending on which interconnection the service token is associated to.|
|service_token_type|[FabricServiceToken_service_token_type](#schemafabricservicetoken_service_token_type)|false|none|Either 'a_side' or 'z_side', depending on which type of Fabric VC was requested.|
|state|[FabricServiceToken_state](#schemafabricservicetoken_state)|false|none|The state of the service token that corresponds with the service<br>token state on Fabric. An 'inactive' state refers to a token that has not been<br>redeemed yet on the Fabric side, an 'active' state refers to a token that has<br>already been redeemed, and an 'expired' state refers to a token that has reached<br>its expiry time.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|role|primary|
|role|secondary|
|service_token_type|a_side|
|service_token_type|z_side|
|state|inactive|
|state|active|
|state|expired|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|contact_email|string|false|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|facility|[Href](#schemahref)|false|none|none|
|id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|metro|object|false|none|The location of where the shared or Dedicated Port is located. For interconnections with Dedicated Ports,<br>  this will be the location of the Dedicated Ports. For Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), this is where interconnection will be originating from, as we pre-authorize the use of one of our shared ports<br>  as the origin of the interconnection using A-Side service tokens. We only allow local connections for Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), so the destination location must be the same as the origin. For Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed), <br>  this will be the destination of the interconnection. We allow remote connections for Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed), so the origin of the interconnection can be a different metro set here.|
|mode|[Interconnection_mode](#schemainterconnection_mode)|false|none|The mode of the interconnection (only relevant to Dedicated Ports). Shared connections won't have this field. Can be either 'standard' or 'tunnel'.<br>  The default mode of an interconnection on a Dedicated Port is 'standard'. The mode can only be changed when there are no associated virtual circuits on the interconnection.<br>  In tunnel mode, an 802.1q tunnel is added to a port to send/receive double tagged packets from server instances.|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|organization|[Href](#schemahref)|false|none|none|
|ports|[[InterconnectionPort](#schemainterconnectionport)]|false|none|For Fabric VCs, these represent Virtual Port(s) created for the interconnection. For dedicated interconnections, these represent the Dedicated Port(s).|
|redundancy|[Interconnection_redundancy](#schemainterconnection_redundancy)|false|none|Either 'primary', meaning a single interconnection, or 'redundant', meaning a redundant interconnection.|
|service_tokens|[[FabricServiceToken](#schemafabricservicetoken)]|false|none|For Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), this will show details of the A-Side service tokens issued for the interconnection. For Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed), this will show the details of the Z-Side service tokens issued for the interconnection. Dedicated interconnections will not have any service tokens issued. There will be one per interconnection, so for redundant interconnections, there should be two service tokens issued.|
|speed|integer|false|none|For interconnections on Dedicated Ports and shared connections, this represents the interconnection's speed in bps. For Fabric VCs, this field refers to the maximum speed of the interconnection in bps. This value will default to 10Gbps for Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed).|
|status|string|false|none|none|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|
|token|string(uuid)|false|none|This token is used for shared interconnections to be used as the Fabric Token. This field is entirely deprecated.|
|type|[Interconnection_type](#schemainterconnection_type)|false|none|The 'shared' type of interconnection refers to shared connections, or later also known as Fabric Virtual Connections (or Fabric VCs). The 'dedicated' type of interconnection refers to interconnections created with Dedicated Ports.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|requested_by|[Href](#schemahref)|false|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|standard|
|mode|tunnel|
|redundancy|primary|
|redundancy|redundant|
|type|shared|
|type|dedicated|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ip_reservation_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The UUID of an IP reservation that belongs to the same project as where the metal gateway will be created in. This field is required unless the private IPv4 subnet size is specified.|
|private_ipv4_subnet_size|integer|false|none|The subnet size (8, 16, 32, 64, or 128) of the private IPv4 reservation that will be created for the metal gateway. This field is required unless a project IP reservation was specified.<br>          Please keep in mind that the number of private metal gateway ranges are limited per project. If you would like to increase the limit per project, please contact support for assistance.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contact_email|string(email)|false|none|The preferred email used for communication and notifications about the Equinix Fabric interconnection. Required when using a Project API key. Optional and defaults to the primary user email address when using a User API key.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|metro|string|true|none|A Metro ID or code. When creating Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), this is where interconnection will be originating from, as we pre-authorize the use of one of our shared ports as the origin of the interconnection using A-Side service tokens. We only allow local connections for Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), so the destination location must be the same as the origin. For Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed), or shared connections, this will be the destination of the interconnection. We allow remote connections for Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed), so the origin of the interconnection can be a different metro set here.|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|project|string|false|none|none|
|redundancy|string|true|none|Either 'primary' or 'redundant'.|
|service_token_type|[VlanFabricVcCreateInput_service_token_type](#schemavlanfabricvccreateinput_service_token_type)|true|none|Either 'a_side' or 'z_side'. Setting this field to 'a_side' will create an interconnection with Fabric VCs (Metal Billed). Setting this field to 'z_side' will create an interconnection with Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed). This is required when the 'type' is 'shared', but this is not applicable when the 'type' is 'dedicated'. This parameter is included in the specification as a developer preview and is generally unavailable. Please contact our Support team for more details.|
|speed|integer|false|none|A interconnection speed, in bps, mbps, or gbps. For Fabric VCs, this represents the maximum speed of the interconnection. For Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), this can only be one of the following: <br>''50mbps'', ''200mbps'', ''500mbps'', ''1gbps'', ''2gbps'', ''5gbps'' or ''10gbps'', and is required for creation. For Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed), this field will always default to ''10gbps'' even if it is not provided.<br>For example, ''500000000'', ''50m'', or' ''500mbps'' will all work as valid inputs.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|
|type|[VlanFabricVcCreateInput_type](#schemavlanfabricvccreateinput_type)|true|none|When requesting for a Fabric VC, the value of this field should be 'shared'.|
|vlans|[integer]|false|none|A list of one or two metro-based VLANs that will be set on the virtual circuits of primary and/or secondary (if redundant) interconnections respectively when creating Fabric VCs. VLANs can also be set after the interconnection is created, but are required to fully activate the virtual circuits.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|service_token_type|a_side|
|service_token_type|z_side|
|type|shared|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bill|boolean|false|none|True if the Virtual Circuit is being billed. Currently, only Virtual Circuits of Fabric VCs (Metal Billed) will be billed. Usage will start the first time the Virtual Circuit becomes active, and will not stop until it is deleted from Metal.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|nni_vlan|integer|false|none|none|
|port|[Href](#schemahref)|false|none|none|
|project|[Href](#schemahref)|false|none|none|
|speed|integer|false|none|For Virtual Circuits on shared and dedicated connections, this speed should match the one set on their Interconnection Ports. For Virtual Circuits on Fabric VCs (both Metal and Fabric Billed) that have found their corresponding Fabric connection, this is the actual speed of the interconnection that was configured when setting up the interconnection on the Fabric Portal. Details on Fabric VCs are included in the specification as a developer preview and is generally unavailable. Please contact our Support team for more details.|
|status|[VlanVirtualCircuit_status](#schemavlanvirtualcircuit_status)|false|none|The status of a Virtual Circuit is always 'pending' on creation. The status can turn to 'Waiting on Customer VLAN' if a Metro VLAN was not set yet on the Virtual Circuit and is the last step needed for full activation. For Dedicated interconnections, as long as the Dedicated Port has been associated to the Virtual Circuit and a NNI VNID has been set, it will turn to 'waiting_on_customer_vlan'. For Fabric VCs, it will only change to 'waiting_on_customer_vlan' once the corresponding Fabric connection has been found on the Fabric side. If the Fabric service token associated with the Virtual Circuit hasn't been redeemed on Fabric within the expiry time, it will change to an `expired` status. Once a Metro VLAN is set on the Virtual Circuit (which for Fabric VCs, can be set on creation of a Fabric VC) and the necessary set up is done, it will turn into 'Activating' status as it tries to activate the Virtual Circuit. Once the Virtual Circuit fully activates and is configured on the switch, it will turn to staus 'active'. For Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), we will start billing the moment the status of the Virtual Circuit turns to 'active'. If there are any changes to the VLAN after the Virtual Circuit is in an 'active' status, the status will show 'changing_vlan' if a new VLAN has been provided, or 'deactivating' if we are removing the VLAN. When a deletion request is issued for the Virtual Circuit, it will move to a 'deleting' status, and we will immediately unconfigure the switch for the Virtual Circuit and issue a deletion on any associated Fabric connections. Any associated Metro VLANs on the virtual circuit will also be unassociated after the switch has been successfully unconfigured. If there are any associated Fabric connections, we will only fully delete the Virtual Circuit once we have checked that the Fabric connection was fully deprovisioned on Fabric.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|
|type|[VlanVirtualCircuit_type](#schemavlanvirtualcircuit_type)|false|none|none|
|virtual_network|[Href](#schemahref)|false|none|none|
|vnid|integer|false|none|none|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|waiting_on_customer_vlan|
|status|activating|
|status|changing_vlan|
|status|deactivating|
|status|deleting|
|status|active|
|status|expired|
|status|activation_failed|
|status|changing_vlan_failed|
|status|deactivation_failed|
|status|delete_failed|
|type|vlan|

Setting this field to 'a_side' will create an interconnection with Fabric VCs (Metal Billed). Setting this field to 'z_side' will create an interconnection with Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed). This is required when the 'type' is 'shared', but this is not applicable when the 'type' is 'dedicated'. This parameter is included in the specification as a developer preview and is generally unavailable. Please contact our Support team for more details.|
|speed|integer|false|none|A interconnection speed, in bps, mbps, or gbps. For Fabric VCs, this represents the maximum speed of the interconnection. For Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), this can only be one of the following: <br>''50mbps'', ''200mbps'', ''500mbps'', ''1gbps'', ''2gbps'', ''5gbps'' or ''10gbps'', and is required for creation. For Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed), this field will always default to ''10gbps'' even if it is not provided.<br>For example, ''500000000'', ''50m'', or' ''500mbps'' will all work as valid inputs.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|
|type|[VlanFabricVcCreateInput_type](#schemavlanfabricvccreateinput_type)|true|none|When requesting for a Fabric VC, the value of this field should be 'shared'.|
|vrfs|[string(uuid)]|true|none|This field holds a list of VRF UUIDs that will be set automatically on the virtual circuits of Fabric VCs on creation, and can hold up to two UUIDs. Two UUIDs are required when requesting redundant Fabric VCs. The first UUID will be set on the primary virtual circuit, while the second UUID will be set on the secondary. The two UUIDs can be the same if both the primary and secondary virtual circuits will be in the same VRF. This parameter is included in the specification as a developer preview and is generally unavailable. Please contact our Support team for more details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|service_token_type|a_side|
|service_token_type|z_side|
|type|shared|

<h2 id="tocS_VrfIpRangeCreateInput">VrfIpRangeCreateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavrfiprangecreateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_VrfIpRangeCreateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSvrfiprangecreateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsvrfiprangecreateinput"></a>

```json
[
  "string"
]
```

A list of CIDR network addresses. Like ["10.0.0.0/16", "2001:d78::/56"]. IPv4 blocks must be between /8 and /29 in size. IPv6 blocks must be between /56 and /64. A VRF\'s IP ranges must be defined in order to create VRF IP Reservations, which can then be used for Metal Gateways or Virtual Circuits.

<h2 id="tocS_VrfIpRangeUpdateInput">VrfIpRangeUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavrfiprangeupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_VrfIpRangeUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSvrfiprangeupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsvrfiprangeupdateinput"></a>

```json
[
  "string"
]
```

A list of CIDR network addresses. Like ["10.0.0.0/16", "2001:d78::/56"]. IPv4 blocks must be between /8 and /29 in size. IPv6 blocks must be between /56 and /64. A VRF\'s IP ranges must be defined in order to create VRF IP Reservations, which can then be used for Metal Gateways or Virtual Circuits. Adding a new CIDR address to the list will result in the creation of a new IP Range for this VRF. Removal of an existing CIDR address from the list will result in the deletion of an existing IP Range for this VRF. Deleting an IP Range will result in the deletion of any VRF IP Reservations contained within the IP Range, as well as the VRF IP Reservation\'s associated Metal Gateways or Virtual Circuits. If you do not wish to add or remove IP Ranges, either include the full existing list of IP Ranges in the update request, or do not specify the `ip_ranges` field in the update request. Specifying a value of `[]` will remove all existing IP Ranges from the VRF.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ip_reservation_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The UUID an a VRF IP Reservation that belongs to the same project as the one in which the Metal Gateway is to be created. Additionally, the VRF IP Reservation and the Virtual Network must reside in the same Metro.|
|virtual_network_id|string(uuid)|true|none|THe UUID of a Metro Virtual Network that belongs to the same project as the one in which the Metal Gateway is to be created. Additionally, the Virtual Network and the VRF IP Reservation must reside in the same metro.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|The unique identifier for the newly-created resource|
|status|[VrfRoute_status](#schemavrfroute_status)|false|read-only|The status of the route. Potential values are "pending", "active", "deleting", and "error", representing various lifecycle states of the route and whether or not it has been successfully configured on the network|
|prefix|string|false|none|The IPv4 prefix for the route, in CIDR-style notation|
|next_hop|string(ipv4)|false|none|The next-hop IPv4 address for the route|
|type|[VrfRoute_type](#schemavrfroute_type)|false|read-only|VRF route type, like 'bgp', 'connected', and 'static'. Currently, only static routes are supported|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|none|
|metal_gateway|[VrfMetalGateway](#schemavrfmetalgateway)|false|none|none|
|virtual_network|[VirtualNetwork](#schemavirtualnetwork)|false|none|none|
|vrf|[Vrf](#schemavrf)|false|none|none|
|href|string|false|read-only|none|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|active|
|status|deleting|
|status|error|
|type|static|

<h2 id="tocS_VrfUpdateInput">VrfUpdateInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavrfupdateinput"></a>
<a id="schema_VrfUpdateInput"></a>
<a id="tocSvrfupdateinput"></a>
<a id="tocsvrfupdateinput"></a>

```json
{
  "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_export_route_map": true,
  "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_bfd_enabled": true,
  "ip_ranges": [
    "ip_ranges",
    "ip_ranges"
  ],
  "local_asn": 0,
  "name": "name",
  "bgp_dynamic_neighbors_enabled": true,
  "description": "description",
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bgp_dynamic_neighbors_enabled|boolean|false|none|Toggle to enable the dynamic bgp neighbors feature on the VRF|
|bgp_dynamic_neighbors_export_route_map|boolean|false|none|Toggle to export the VRF route-map to the dynamic bgp neighbors|
|bgp_dynamic_neighbors_bfd_enabled|boolean|false|none|Toggle BFD on dynamic bgp neighbors sessions|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|ip_ranges|[string]|false|none|A list of CIDR network addresses. Like ["10.0.0.0/16", "2001:d78::/56"]. IPv4 blocks must be between /8 and /29 in size. IPv6 blocks must be between /56 and /64. A VRF\'s IP ranges must be defined in order to create VRF IP Reservations, which can then be used for Metal Gateways or Virtual Circuits. Adding a new CIDR address to the list will result in the creation of a new IP Range for this VRF. Removal of an existing CIDR address from the list will result in the deletion of an existing IP Range for this VRF. Deleting an IP Range will result in the deletion of any VRF IP Reservations contained within the IP Range, as well as the VRF IP Reservation\'s associated Metal Gateways or Virtual Circuits. If you do not wish to add or remove IP Ranges, either include the full existing list of IP Ranges in the update request, or do not specify the `ip_ranges` field in the update request. Specifying a value of `[]` will remove all existing IP Ranges from the VRF.|
|local_asn|integer(int32)|false|none|The new `local_asn` value for the VRF. This field cannot be updated when there are active Interconnection Virtual Circuits associated to the VRF, or if any of the VLANs of the VRF's metal gateway has been assigned on an instance.|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer_ip|string|false|none|An IP address from the subnet that will be used on the Customer side. This parameter is optional, but if supplied, we will use the other usable IP address in the subnet as the Metal IP. By default, the last usable IP address in the subnet will be used.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|md5|string|false|none|The MD5 password for the BGP peering in plaintext (not a checksum).|
|metal_ip|string|false|none|An IP address from the subnet that will be used on the Metal side. This parameter is optional, but if supplied, we will use the other usable IP address in the subnet as the Customer IP. By default, the first usable IP address in the subnet will be used.|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|port|[Href](#schemahref)|false|none|none|
|nni_vlan|integer|false|none|none|
|peer_asn|integer|false|none|The peer ASN that will be used with the VRF on the Virtual Circuit.|
|project|[Href](#schemahref)|false|none|none|
|speed|integer|false|none|integer representing bps speed|
|status|[VrfVirtualCircuit_status](#schemavrfvirtualcircuit_status)|false|none|The status changes of a VRF virtual circuit are generally the same as Virtual Circuits that aren't in a VRF. However, for VRF Virtual Circuits on Fabric VCs, the status will change to 'waiting_on_peering_details' once the Fabric service token associated with the virtual circuit has been redeemed on Fabric, and Metal has found the associated Fabric connection. At this point, users can update the subnet, MD5 password, customer IP and/or metal IP accordingly. For VRF Virtual Circuits on Dedicated Ports, we require all peering details to be set on creation of a VRF Virtual Circuit. The status will change to `changing_peering_details` whenever an active VRF Virtual Circuit has any of its peering details updated.|
|subnet|string|false|none|The /30 or /31 subnet of one of the VRF IP Blocks that will be used with the VRF for the Virtual Circuit. This subnet does not have to be an existing VRF IP reservation, as we will create the VRF IP reservation on creation if it does not exist. The Metal IP and Customer IP must be IPs from this subnet. For /30 subnets, the network and broadcast IPs cannot be used as the Metal or Customer IP.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|customer_ip|string|false|none|An IP address from the subnet that will be used on the Customer side. This parameter is optional, but if supplied, we will use the other usable IP address in the subnet as the Metal IP. By default, the last usable IP address in the subnet will be used.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|md5|string \| null|false|none|The plaintext BGP peering password shared by neighbors as an MD5 checksum:<br>* must be 10-20 characters long<br>* may not include punctuation<br>* must be a combination of numbers and letters<br>* must contain at least one lowercase, uppercase, and digit character<br>|
|metal_ip|string|false|none|An IP address from the subnet that will be used on the Metal side. This parameter is optional, but if supplied, we will use the other usable IP address in the subnet as the Customer IP. By default, the first usable IP address in the subnet will be used.|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|nni_vlan|integer|true|none|none|
|peer_asn|integer|true|none|The peer ASN that will be used with the VRF on the Virtual Circuit.|
|project_id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|speed|integer|false|none|speed can be passed as integer number representing bps speed or string (e.g. '52m' or '100g' or '4 gbps')|
|subnet|string|true|none|The /30 or /31 subnet of one of the VRF IP Blocks that will be used with the VRF for the Virtual Circuit. This subnet does not have to be an existing VRF IP reservation, as we will create the VRF IP reservation on creation if it does not exist. The Metal IP and Customer IP must be IPs from this subnet. For /30 subnets, the network and broadcast IPs cannot be used as the Metal or Customer IP. The subnet specified must be contained within an already-defined IP Range for the VRF.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|none|
|vrf|string(uuid)|true|none|The UUID of the VRF that will be associated with the Virtual Circuit.|

```json
"standard"
```

The mode of the interconnection (only relevant to Dedicated Ports). Fabric VCs won't have this field. Can be either 'standard' or 'tunnel'.
  The default mode of an interconnection on a Dedicated Port is 'standard'. The mode can only be changed when there are no associated virtual circuits on the interconnection.
  In tunnel mode, an 802.1q tunnel is added to a port to send/receive double tagged packets from server instances.

<h2 id="tocS_Device_state">Device_state</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadevice_state"></a>
<a id="schema_Device_state"></a>
<a id="tocSdevice_state"></a>
<a id="tocsdevice_state"></a>

```json
"queued"
```

The current state the instance is in.

* When an instance is initially created it will be in the `queued` state until it is picked up by the provisioner.
* Once provisioning has begun on the instance it's state will move to `provisioning`.
* When an instance is deleted, it will move to `deprovisioning` state until the deprovision is completed and the instance state moves to `deleted`.
* If an instance fails to provision or deprovision it will move to `failed` state.
* Once an instance has completed provisioning it will move to `active` state.
* If an instance is currently powering off or powering on it will move to `powering_off` or `powering_on` states respectively. 
* When the instance is powered off completely it will move to the `inactive` state.
* When an instance is powered on completely it will move to the `active` state.
* Using the reinstall action to install a new OS on the instance will cause the instance state to change to `reinstalling`.
* When the reinstall action is complete the instance will move to `active` state.

<h2 id="tocS_Interconnection_mode">Interconnection_mode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainterconnection_mode"></a>
<a id="schema_Interconnection_mode"></a>
<a id="tocSinterconnection_mode"></a>
<a id="tocsinterconnection_mode"></a>

```json
"standard"
```

The mode of the interconnection (only relevant to Dedicated Ports). Shared connections won't have this field. Can be either 'standard' or 'tunnel'.
  The default mode of an interconnection on a Dedicated Port is 'standard'. The mode can only be changed when there are no associated virtual circuits on the interconnection.
  In tunnel mode, an 802.1q tunnel is added to a port to send/receive double tagged packets from server instances.

<h2 id="tocS_Interconnection_redundancy">Interconnection_redundancy</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainterconnection_redundancy"></a>
<a id="schema_Interconnection_redundancy"></a>
<a id="tocSinterconnection_redundancy"></a>
<a id="tocsinterconnection_redundancy"></a>

```json
"primary"
```

Either 'primary', meaning a single interconnection, or 'redundant', meaning a redundant interconnection.

<h2 id="tocS_Interconnection_type">Interconnection_type</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainterconnection_type"></a>
<a id="schema_Interconnection_type"></a>
<a id="tocSinterconnection_type"></a>
<a id="tocsinterconnection_type"></a>

```json
"shared"
```

The 'shared' type of interconnection refers to shared connections, or later also known as Fabric Virtual Connections (or Fabric VCs). The 'dedicated' type of interconnection refers to interconnections created with Dedicated Ports.

<h2 id="tocS_InterconnectionPort_role">InterconnectionPort_role</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainterconnectionport_role"></a>
<a id="schema_InterconnectionPort_role"></a>
<a id="tocSinterconnectionport_role"></a>
<a id="tocsinterconnectionport_role"></a>

```json
"primary"
```

Either 'primary' or 'secondary'.

<h2 id="tocS_InterconnectionPort_status">InterconnectionPort_status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainterconnectionport_status"></a>
<a id="schema_InterconnectionPort_status"></a>
<a id="tocSinterconnectionport_status"></a>
<a id="tocsinterconnectionport_status"></a>

```json
"requested"
```

For both Fabric VCs and Dedicated Ports, this will be 'requested' on creation and 'deleting' on deletion. Once the Fabric VC has found its corresponding Fabric connection, this will turn to 'active'. For Dedicated Ports, once the dedicated port is associated, this will also turn to 'active'. For Fabric VCs, this can turn into an 'expired' state if the service token associated is expired.

<h2 id="tocS_MetalGateway_state">MetalGateway_state</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemametalgateway_state"></a>
<a id="schema_MetalGateway_state"></a>
<a id="tocSmetalgateway_state"></a>
<a id="tocsmetalgateway_state"></a>

```json
"ready"
```

The current state of the Metal Gateway. 'Ready' indicates the gateway record has been configured, but is currently not active on the network. 'Active' indicates the gateway has been configured on the network. 'Deleting' is a temporary state used to indicate that the gateway is in the process of being un-configured from the network, after which the gateway record will be deleted.

<h2 id="tocS_VlanFabricVcCreateInput_service_token_type">VlanFabricVcCreateInput_service_token_type</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavlanfabricvccreateinput_service_token_type"></a>

<a id="tocSvlanfabricvccreateinput_service_token_type"></a>
<a id="tocsvlanfabricvccreateinput_service_token_type"></a>

```json
"a_side"
```

Either 'a_side' or 'z_side'. Setting this field to 'a_side' will create an interconnection with Fabric VCs (Metal Billed). Setting this field to 'z_side' will create an interconnection with Fabric VCs (Fabric Billed). This is required when the 'type' is 'shared', but this is not applicable when the 'type' is 'dedicated'. This parameter is included in the specification as a developer preview and is generally unavailable. Please contact our Support team for more details.

<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<h2 id="tocS_VlanVirtualCircuit_status">VlanVirtualCircuit_status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavlanvirtualcircuit_status"></a>
<a id="schema_VlanVirtualCircuit_status"></a>
<a id="tocSvlanvirtualcircuit_status"></a>
<a id="tocsvlanvirtualcircuit_status"></a>

```json
"pending"
```

The status of a Virtual Circuit is always 'pending' on creation. The status can turn to 'Waiting on Customer VLAN' if a Metro VLAN was not set yet on the Virtual Circuit and is the last step needed for full activation. For Dedicated interconnections, as long as the Dedicated Port has been associated to the Virtual Circuit and a NNI VNID has been set, it will turn to 'waiting_on_customer_vlan'. For Fabric VCs, it will only change to 'waiting_on_customer_vlan' once the corresponding Fabric connection has been found on the Fabric side. If the Fabric service token associated with the Virtual Circuit hasn't been redeemed on Fabric within the expiry time, it will change to an `expired` status. Once a Metro VLAN is set on the Virtual Circuit (which for Fabric VCs, can be set on creation of a Fabric VC) and the necessary set up is done, it will turn into 'Activating' status as it tries to activate the Virtual Circuit. Once the Virtual Circuit fully activates and is configured on the switch, it will turn to staus 'active'. For Fabric VCs (Metal Billed), we will start billing the moment the status of the Virtual Circuit turns to 'active'. If there are any changes to the VLAN after the Virtual Circuit is in an 'active' status, the status will show 'changing_vlan' if a new VLAN has been provided, or 'deactivating' if we are removing the VLAN. When a deletion request is issued for the Virtual Circuit, it will move to a 'deleting' status, and we will immediately unconfigure the switch for the Virtual Circuit and issue a deletion on any associated Fabric connections. Any associated Metro VLANs on the virtual circuit will also be unassociated after the switch has been successfully unconfigured. If there are any associated Fabric connections, we will only fully delete the Virtual Circuit once we have checked that the Fabric connection was fully deprovisioned on Fabric.

<h2 id="tocS_VrfRoute_status">VrfRoute_status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavrfroute_status"></a>
<a id="schema_VrfRoute_status"></a>
<a id="tocSvrfroute_status"></a>
<a id="tocsvrfroute_status"></a>

```json
"active"
```

The status of the route. Potential values are "pending", "active", "deleting", and "error", representing various lifecycle states of the route and whether or not it has been successfully configured on the network

<h2 id="tocS_VrfVirtualCircuit_status">VrfVirtualCircuit_status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavrfvirtualcircuit_status"></a>
<a id="schema_VrfVirtualCircuit_status"></a>
<a id="tocSvrfvirtualcircuit_status"></a>
<a id="tocsvrfvirtualcircuit_status"></a>

```json
"pending"
```

The status changes of a VRF virtual circuit are generally the same as Virtual Circuits that aren't in a VRF. However, for VRF Virtual Circuits on Fabric VCs, the status will change to 'waiting_on_peering_details' once the Fabric service token associated with the virtual circuit has been redeemed on Fabric, and Metal has found the associated Fabric connection. At this point, users can update the subnet, MD5 password, customer IP and/or metal IP accordingly. For VRF Virtual Circuits on Dedicated Ports, we require all peering details to be set on creation of a VRF Virtual Circuit. The status will change to `changing_peering_details` whenever an active VRF Virtual Circuit has any of its peering details updated.
